title: LIMS/ELN Enterprise Implementation 0.3.2 release exemplar
summary: One accepted enterprise implementation release, its observed Git identity, and a complete process-local idempotency file remain inspectable through stable, reproducible coordinates.

use.practicalQuestion: How can another collaboration team inspect an accepted LIMS/ELN implementation release and one consequential mechanism through stable, reproducible coordinates?
use.changedAbility: A collaborator can resolve the release subject, reproduce its Git archive digest, inspect its later release observation, and compare one public Python file byte for byte with the owning release.
readers: AI collaborators orienting to a released enterprise implementation
Technical practitioners evaluating release identity, source authority, and replay boundaries

provenance.description: A Registry discovery projection of an Apache-2.0 release and one byte-identical implementation file. The implementation repository retains release, runtime, test, license, and attribution authority.
provenance.temporalScope: This record binds immutable release v0.3.2 and its later release-observation record. Post-release development and the Program repository's separate release state remain distinct.

technicalVeracity.basis: The implementation repository records an annotated v0.3.2 tag, accepted commit and tree, reproducible Git archive SHA-256, successful hosted validation, and a later verified release observation. The carried idempotency file is byte-identical to the tagged source, and nine selected tests passed against a fresh archive of that exact tag.

reviewQuestions: Which fields form the stable reservation identity?
How does the ledger distinguish exact replay, changed content, and work already in progress?
Which result becomes recoverable after commit?
Which transaction and coordination guarantees move to a durable implementation?
decisionRules: Scope each stable key by tenant before deciding who may execute.
Bind the stable key to a content digest and route changed content to a new command identity.
Return the recorded outcome for an exact completed replay and surface active ownership for pending work.
Restore the complete prior ledger snapshot when the in-memory reference transaction stops.

instructionYields.instruction: Define stable identity, content identity, reservation state, committed outcome, and recovery ownership together.
Exercise exact replay, changed-content collision, in-progress ownership, tenant separation, commit failure, and ambiguous external outcomes.
Preserve the demonstrated decisions while selecting durable uniqueness, isolation, leases, fencing, and restart recovery for the production implementation.

practice.codeExemplarGranularity: One complete 94-line Python file, one machine-readable release coordinate, and exact pointers to nine tests in the accepted implementation release.
practice.complexityAndAllocation: The in-memory ledger uses one tenant-and-key dictionary lookup for reservation and copies its entries for transaction snapshots. A durable implementation owns storage, concurrency, lease, fencing, and restart behavior.

boundaries.evidence: The record establishes the named Git objects, reproducible archive digest, later release observation, nine-test exact-tag result, and byte identity of the carried source file. Complete implementation behavior remains established by the owning repository's release validation and tests.
boundaries.trust: The checked release observation records valid merge and annotated-tag verification; local SHA-256 and Git-object comparisons reproduce the release archive and selected files. Configured environments and accountable production acceptance remain with their named owners.
boundaries.transfer: A receiving team returns to the exact owning release, its tests, and its release documentation before adapting the excerpt, then selects a durable synchronization and transaction model for multi-process use.

failureModes: A copied source file can drift from the immutable release while retaining a familiar path.
A release tag, later observation, license file, and attribution file can be collapsed into one incomplete coordinate.
A process-local dictionary can be mistaken for durable multi-process coordination.
A stable key bound only to caller identity can replay changed work as though it were the original command.
recoveryMoves: Reproduce the recorded source SHA-256 and Git blob before accepting a copied representation.
Resolve the release subject and later observation independently, then compare every named file digest.
Return durability, isolation, lease, fencing, and restart claims to the database-backed implementation.
Bind stable identity to semantic content and allocate a new command identity when that content changes.

relationships.reason: The implementation repository retains the accepted release, complete runtime, tests, and release evidence.
The Program hub can link this Registry coordinate after the selected public projection is accepted.
This first repository exemplar exercises external release coordinates through the existing extension envelope before a shared schema field is promoted.
